solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slave back in shifting coal out of doors

indicators.note: in tells us the slave piece sits inside the jumbled coal letters
shifting means the letters of coal move into a new order
back tells us the word for slave is read from right to left

parts.note: a serf is a feudal labourer bound to the land, so a slave

explanation.surface: Someone moving coal outdoors with a slave helping at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slave back' reads like a slave returning; in fact 'back' turns the slave word round before 'in' places it among the jumbled coal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian borrowing describes something done in the open air, such as eating outside.

clue.text: A lot of words about musical work may be to the point

indicators.note: about means the opening pieces go around the musical work
a lot of something is most of it, so the last letter of the words piece goes

parts.note: prose is written words, as opposed to verse
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Plenty of text discussing a composition may be relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' of 'A lot of' does double duty in the surface but gives its own letter here, while 'lot of' trims the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent or relevant is said to be fitting, from the French for 'to the purpose'.

clue.text: Peel having something false about Liberal

indicators.note: about means the false thing goes around the letter for Liberal

parts.note: a fake is something false
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: Sounds like a politician named Peel being phoney about the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel' suggests Sir Robert Peel the statesman, but it is a verb meaning to come off in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint or skin that comes away in thin pieces is said to peel off, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Replaces taxi after crash? Wonderful

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters of replaces taxi are scrambled

explanation.surface: Getting a new cab after an accident would be marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges REPLACESTAXI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exceptionally good beyond the ordinary is a colloquial term for marvellous.

clue.text: Company's first member to head for the top

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the company word is used

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: The firm's leading member aiming to get to the top job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes C from 'Company's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend a mountain or ladder is to go upwards to its summit.

clue.text: Rejection of plans for annoying emails

indicators.note: a rejection throws something back, so the word for plans is read backwards

parts.note: maps are plans or charts of an area

explanation.surface: Turning down proposals because of irritating junk mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejection of' turns MAPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited bulk messages filling an inbox are known by this name, borrowed from tinned meat.

clue.text: Foresee alcoholic drink turning up in pint container?

indicators.note: in tells us the drink sits within the pint abbreviation

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for pint, here acting as the container

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means the drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Seeing ahead that someone's drink will be upended in a pint glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pint container' suggests a glass, but it is the abbreviation for pint acting as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast what will happen is to see it before it comes, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Magnate's way of working? Ear pricked up

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

indicators.note: in a down answer pricked up means the ear word rises, read upwards

parts.note: lug is slang for an ear

explanation.surface: A tycoon's method of operating involves listening attentively.
explanation.walkthrough: LUG is British slang for an ear; 'pricked up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful business tycoon, originally a Mughal emperor, is a synonym for a magnate.

clue.text: Outstanding: another century, then adding single

parts.note: a second one is another
a ton is a hundred, a century
one is single

explanation.surface: A cricketer's great innings: another hundred, then one more run.
explanation.walkthrough: A century in cricket is a hundred runs, also called a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning better than anything else, unbeaten by any rival.

clue.text: Nonsense written about a small Sunday meal

indicators.note: written about means the nonsense word is set around the following letters

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A critic penning rubbish about a modest Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' puts A and S inside ROT. A traditional British Sunday lunch is a joint of meat cooked in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of oven-cooked meat is the classic British Sunday lunch dish, an example of the meal.

clue.text: Recalled diving bird going behind one cold Arctic feature

indicators.note: going behind places the bird piece after the letters for one and cold

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
C stands for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: Remembering a seabird diving behind something cold in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diving bird' is one unit naming a species of water bird, not a bird plus a separate action.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge floating mass of ice broken off a glacier, typical of polar waters.

clue.text: Baked food? Large quantity, not left

indicators.note: not means the letter for left is taken away

parts.note: a pile is a large amount, as in a pile of money

explanation.surface: Asking whether a big helping of baked goods has been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes L from PILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry case with a filling, cooked in the oven, is a kind of baked food.

clue.text: Brothers I found in care of revolutionary priest of heavenly aspect

indicators.note: being found in someone's care means held within them, so the brothers and I sit inside
revolutionary means turning round, so the priest word is read backwards

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
BROS is the short form of brothers, as in a company name

explanation.surface: A sibling discovered under the protection of a rebel cleric with a saintly look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'care of' looks like the postal C/O, but here 'found in care of' only signals that the brothers sit inside the turned-round priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, so the adjective means divinely delicious or godlike.

clue.text: Sheltered area is covered by agent not fully alert

indicators.note: being covered by something means being enclosed within it, so the sheltered area goes inside the agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A secret agent watching a hidden spot while barely awake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drowsy and half-awake is only partly alert, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Watch British quarrel that's curiously raised?

parts.note: to eye is to watch
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Seeing a British argument that has oddly flared up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' seems to mean 'strangely', but it means 'in curiosity'.
explanation.definitionFit: This facial feature is lifted when someone is inquisitive or surprised.

clue.text: Newspaperman recalled repetition about one day

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
about means the repetition word goes around the letters for one and day

parts.note: rote is learning by repetition
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A journalist remembering the same thing happening one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and D inside ROTE to make ROIDTE, and 'recalled' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper's content is its chief journalist, a newspaperman.

clue.text: Others adopting physical exercise about to get appreciation

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the others word holds the following letters

parts.note: the rest are the others
PE is physical education, exercise at school
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Other people taking up exercise in order to earn admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: High regard or esteem for someone is a synonym for valuing them.

clue.text: Soccer playing about to finish leading to increasing noise

indicators.note: about means the jumbled soccer letters go around the word for finish
playing means the letters of soccer are moved about into a new order

parts.note: to finish is to end

explanation.surface: A football match nearing its close leads to a rising roar from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is not part of the anagram signal: 'playing' alone scrambles the football word, which then goes around the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for a gradual rise in loudness, used generally for a build-up of sound.

clue.text: Six in California make petty complaints

indicators.note: in tells us the six goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Half a dozen people in California grumbling about trifles.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise trivial objections is to quibble, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Looking swanky a couple of times in US city

indicators.note: in tells us the middle letters go inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
T is short for time, so two of them make TT

explanation.surface: Appearing stylish on a few occasions in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and neatly dressed, a synonym for dapper or stylish in appearance.

clue.text: He perhaps requires odd bits of glass

indicators.note: odd bits means the first, third and fifth letters of glass are taken

explanation.surface: A man apparently needing scattered fragments of glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man, but it is the chemical symbol for helium.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium, symbol He, is an example of a substance in its vapour state at room temperature.

clue.text: Mostly vague when stewing a fruit

indicators.note: stewing stirs things together, so the letters are mixed into a new order
mostly means all but the final letter of vague is kept

explanation.surface: Being rather unclear while cooking some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims VAGUE to VAGU, and 'stewing' rearranges VAGU plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical produce with pink or white flesh, an example of the category.

clue.text: TV Andre recycled, being green

indicators.note: recycled means the letters of TV Andre are reused in a new order

explanation.surface: A TV personality called Andre being environmentally minded by recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges TVANDRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush with vegetation, a synonym for grassy-coloured or leafy.

clue.text: Make speech over level of tax?

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a tax rate is the level at which tax is charged

explanation.surface: A politician giving an address about the tax rate.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end, written O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a formal address, often pompously, is a verb synonym for speaking publicly.

clue.text: Rule applied to new part of garden

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A regulation imposed on a new section of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of mown grass is a typical feature of a garden.

clue.text: Always getting the same part of cooked pasty etc.

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of pasty etc are prepared into a new order

explanation.surface: Always being served the same piece of a baked pasty and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: A pasty is a British pastry filled with meat and vegetables; 'cooked' rearranges PASTYETC.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor repeatedly given similar roles is said to be pigeonholed in that way.
